Model the combustion chamber as a 2D axisymmetric wedge of 5 degrees with an axial length of 0.2 m and a radius of 0.05 m.
Use a mesh with 100 cells in the axial direction and 50 cells in the radial direction, graded finer near the axis and near the injector face.
Use OpenFOAM's reactingParcelFoam solver with a k-epsilon turbulence model.
Set the chamber initially filled with hot air at 800 K and 101325 Pa, at rest, with species mass fractions O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767.
Set the co-flow air inlet velocity to U = (10, 0, 0) m/s, temperature to 800 K, pressure to 101325 Pa, and species mass fractions to O2 = 0.233 and N2 = 0.767.
Set the inlet turbulence intensity to 5% and the turbulent length scale to 7% of the inlet diameter, giving k = 0.375 m2/s2 and epsilon = 5.36 m2/s3.
Set the chamber wall to no-slip velocity and fixed temperature 400 K.
Set the outlet to zero-gradient for velocity and temperature and fixed pressure 101325 Pa.
Inject liquid n-dodecane at 0.002 kg/s using a cone injection model located at the center of the inlet.
Set the droplet temperature to 300 K.
Use a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m.
Use a cone angle of 20 degrees as a reasonable assumed default because no cone angle was specified.
Use the standard drag model and the RanzMarshall heat and mass transfer model for the spray.
Use finite-rate gas-phase chemistry with a two-step global reaction mechanism for n-dodecane, configured in constant/combustionProperties and constant/reactionSchemes.
Use janaf thermodynamics for the species.
